svg.text: Episode 6 - friction-circle usage along the corner
Rear-wheel drive 12.09 s, front-wheel drive 12.05 s over 393 m. Shaded band is the corner; everything right of it is the exit straight.

Through the corner both cars are at the limit -- every wheel near 1.0 -- and the lines are nearly identical. The difference is entirely on the exit, where the front-wheel-drive car's front tires must steer and accelerate at once and reach 61% average usage against the rear-drive car's 9%.

Caveat on record: the rear-drive solve reported 'Solve_Succeeded'. Its objective was stable and its envelope occupancy zero, so it is converged in practice, but it is not a clean exit and the -0.03 s gap should be read as approximate.

[MEASURED] double-track model + optimal control + Sedan_Pac02Tire.tir - offsets removed - m 1360 kg - 54% front - 100 nodes - [SOURCED] RV-1 params §1 - IDEAL differential [ASSUMED]: torque split floats freely, the best an LSD could manage. See figure 03 for the open-diff case
Both solves constrain slip angle to +/-12 deg and every wheel's longitudinal force to its own capability. Envelope occupancy is zero in both, so neither answer relies on extrapolating the tire model.
